scenes.headline: How BPE got faster, and why 'the' takes six rows
scenes.sub: Hugging Face tokenizers v1 and Combinatorial BPE
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mulberry! Two tokenizer releases, one week. One makes byte pair encoding faster. The other asks why one word takes six rows.

scenes.text: Tokenizers v1 keeps every token ID and rebuilds the engine. Combinatorial BPE stores each word once and adds space and case as modifiers.
scenes.say: Hugging Face kept every token ID and rebuilt the engine. Combinatorial BPE stores each word once, plus modifiers.

items.say: Start from the two hundred fifty-six byte values, so any text encodes.
A fixed regular expression cuts the text, and each word keeps the space before it.
Then merge the lowest-ranked pair, again and again.

steps.say: The split drops the regex engine: a bitstream program decides sixty-four bytes per register operation.
Each piece checks a word cache, so a repeated word skips merging.
New words go through a merge loop that never allocates.
The output is unchanged: twenty million tokens, and every ID matched.

scenes.title: Measured speedup on one core, GPT-2
scenes.say: On one busy core, English encoded about forty-one times faster, Hindi fifty-four, Chinese nineteen.

scenes.title: One token, four parts
scenes.say: Combinatorial BPE splits every token into four parts.

parts.note: hand-coded: as-is, Capitalised or all caps
parts.say: A hand-coded variation: as is, capitalised, or all caps.

parts.note: learned: a space, a bracket, a quote
parts.say: A learned prefix, like a leading space.
A core, from ordinary byte pair encoding on lower-cased words.
And a learned suffix of punctuation.

steps.say: Five spellings of the share one core row.
The four tables split one budget of rows.
The model sums four embeddings in, and predicts the four parts out in turn.

scenes.label: of Llama 3's vocabulary is space and case variants of other rows
scenes.say: The waste is real: almost a quarter of Llama 3's vocabulary is space and case copies of other rows.

scenes.text: Tokenizers v1 made BPE fast without changing an ID. Combinatorial BPE asks whether the IDs were right.
scenes.say: Tokenizers v1 made byte pair encoding fast without changing an ID. Combinatorial BPE asks whether the IDs were right.
To recap: same IDs from a rebuilt engine, and six rows for one word, folded into one.
